newsitem.title: USA: Crude prices flatten gains, grades hold strength.
newsitem.headline: Crude prices flatten gains, grades hold strength.

text.p: U.S. cash crude prices faded from earlier gains mid-afternoon Thursday, but the domestic grade sector retained momentum.
Cash dealers in the Gulf said it seems the supply overhang has lifted to a degree, allowing stronger differentials for both sweet and sour barrels.
"You've got West African heading to the Far East, the Cusiana is down to two, so things look like they're getting cleaned up," said a cash trader.
Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James remained at a 22-24 cents premium to September WTI, West Texas Sour/Midland at $1.34-31 under the benchmark and Midland/WTI at -34/32 cents.
Benchmark crude for September stood 10 cents lower at $20.05-15 a barrel, with the September/October roll at -21/19 cents.

North Sea crude prices pushed sweet U.S. barrels to firmer numbers as well. Dated Brent for August 28-30 delivery sold at September Brent -5 cents and a second deal was done for the September 5-7 window at benchmark Brent -7 cents, an average of six cents firmer than Wednesday levels.
